newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty softens vs basket of currencies, depos flat.
newsitem.headline: Zloty softens vs basket of currencies, depos flat.

text.p: The Polish zloty eased versus the basket of currencies as small currency buying orders coming from oil sector importers established a currency-buying trend in early trade, dealers said.
They said that after this morning decline, the zloty traded relatively steady for the rest of the day following dollar/mark moves on world markets.

"A light currency buying trend formed on the back of orders from oil-importers, but it soon faded and the zloty was left to track dollar/mark moves for the rest of the day," said Tomasz Nowakowski, forex dealer at Bank Handlowy SA.
The zloty was at 2.8112/16 per dollar, down from 2.8055/70 on Tuesday and at 1.8420/35 to the mark, down from 1.8393/19.
It closed at 1.74/1.69 percent below the centre of the 14-percent trading band against Tuesday's close at 1.88/1.76 percent from the parity rate.

On the money market one-day rates inched down slightly from Tuesday's levels but remained above the main 14-day drainage rate of 19.14 percent as lenders were reluctant to lower prices despite the early stages of the monthly reserve period.
Overnight rates were at 20.5/20.9 percent against 20.6/20.7 at 0630 GMT and down at offer from Tuesday's 19.95/21.05.

Dealers said tomorrow/next rates rose about half a point after the central bank announced the results of Wednesday's reverse repo and NBP-bill auctions, which will drain a combined 694 million zlotys on Thursday.
"T/N rates broke out of a gradual downward trend when the results of today's open market operations were announced," said Krzysztof Chmura, dealer at Bank Gdanski SA.
T/N rates closed at 20.5/20.9 percent, after hitting lows around 19.7/20.2 percent, and down from Tuesday's 20.30/21.20.
The National Bank of Poland sold 300 million zlotys of its 273-day bills and the average yield rose 0.03 to 19.93 percent.
The NBP also drained 394 million zlotys for 14 days and the maximum accepted rate inched up 0.01 to 19.14 percent.
On Wednesday the central bank announced that it raised the average monthly reserve money target for October to 32.95-33.65 billion zlotys from 32.54-33.24 billion in September.
The average monthly level of reserve money is the NBP's key monetary policy goal this year through which it strives to control broad money growth and price growth.
